subject: scientist
label: scientist, in the place of the game's models/scientist.mdl

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/houndeye.mdl, models/gman.mdl, models/hassassin.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The brief's words (older man, lab coat, tie, trousers, glasses, grey hair, about 68 tall) read as a man in a coat, but the outline is off in the side and back views (LEFT, RIGHT, BACK): a grey box sits on top of and behind the head, and the shoulder blocks stick out past the coat in the top view. Those are outline faults, not paint.

M2.reason: Measured height is 68.2 against the brief's 68 (within 0.3%). Length 11.8 and width 28.8 are not given by the brief and are not charged.

M3.reason: Every part the brief names is there: lab coat, light blue shirt collar, red tie, square breast pocket, dark trousers, dark glasses, brown shoes, skin hands, and a grey mass for hair. Nothing is missing. The grey hair is a flat box above and behind the head (FRONT, LEFT, BACK), not hair, and the shoulder pieces are cylinders, so the shape of those parts is wrong.

M4.reason: Colours follow the brief: white coat, red tie, pink skin, dark grey trousers, brown shoes. Materials read as cloth for the coat and skin for the face and hands.

M5.reason: The coat carries a blotchy grey mottling across the whole coat in every view (FRONT, BACK, FRONT-LEFT), which reads as a smear or noise rather than cloth weave or lab-coat seams. The brief asks for no markings, so the detail is judged only as it looks; it looks wrong.

M6.reason: Beside Half-Life's own humans in lineup.png (B, C), the asset is visibly blockier and lower in detail: flat box shapes, a grey box head, and no facial features beyond the glasses. A player would not take it for one of the game's, though it is recognisably a scientist-style NPC.

M7.reason: The front is the front: tie, pocket and glasses face the FRONT view. It stands upright, and the feet sit on the floor line in LEFT and RIGHT, with the origin at the floor.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. Triangles are 432, under twice the Half-Life median of 504 (1008) and under the third quartile of 731. The silhouette shows nothing open or floating.

C1.reason: In motion the body stays together and the legs and arms swing from their joints. In the small frames the shoulder blocks look to lift off the coat in frames 3/22 and 19/22, and the torso does not lean into the run. Resolution is too low to be sure, so this is charged as a fault to check.
